sources.entry: Hosts.prefpane - System preference pane to manage your hosts file. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon] ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]](https://github.com/specialunderwear/Hosts.prefpane)

summary.one_liner: Hosts.prefpane is a macOS system preference pane and companion app for viewing, toggling, adding and removing entries in the /etc/hosts file.
keywords: turn host entries on and off
summary.what_it_does: Adds a preference pane to macOS System Preferences that lists the entries in /etc/hosts and lets you switch each one on or off, add new ones, and remove existing ones. When an entry is toggled off, it is removed from the hosts file and kept in the app's own preferences storage rather than being commented out. Comments in the hosts file are not shown in the list. Edits made directly to /etc/hosts are detected and merged into the listing. Backups are stored in ~/Library/Application Support/Hosts, including a hosts.orig copy from before first use and a hosts.session backup for each session. Default OS host entries are hidden and cannot be edited. A separate Hosts App is also provided that can run from any location.
use_cases: Turn hosts file entries on and off without editing the file by hand
Block or redirect domains on a Mac via the hosts file
Keep a clean /etc/hosts while storing unused entries elsewhere
Back up and restore the hosts file on macOS
Manage local domain mappings for development on a Mac
how_to_run: Download 'Hosts PrefPane 1.4.5.pkg' (installer for the preference pane) from the author's website and run it, entering admin credentials
Alternatively download 'Hosts App 1.4.5.zip' and run the app from any location
To compile the parser, install bison with 'brew install bison' so it is in /usr/local/opt/bison/bin/
notable: Disabled entries are stored in app preferences instead of being commented out in /etc/hosts
Automatic backups: hosts.orig from before first use and hosts.session per session
Detects and merges direct manual edits to /etc/hosts
Ships as both a preference pane installer and a standalone app
Hides OS-required default host entries so they cannot be broken from the UI
caveats: The preference pane cannot be notarized, so on macOS Catalina and later it must be installed through a separately built installer; the README points to an external guide for this process
Pre-built binaries are hosted on the author's website rather than in the repository
Compiling the parser expects bison at a specific Homebrew path (/usr/local/opt/bison/bin/)
